subject: Intermittent lag on interactive/chat stream — immediate mitigations & playbook
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@novarix.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@novarix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Intermittent lag on interactive/chat stream — immediate mitigations & playbook

Hi Samantha and Daniel,

Thanks again for flagging the elevated latency on Novarix's streaming/chat route this morning. We detected a correlated increase in token-generation latency for the us-west-2 shard between ~08:40–09:05 PT, which aligns with what you reported.

Quick summary of what we've done so far:
- Triaged: identified a subset of requests experiencing repeated retransmit/backpressure inside the serving batcher under a spike of long-context requests.
- Mitigated (hotfix): temporarily enabled per-customer strict-batching caps and routed Novarix traffic to a warm replica pool to reduce queueing.

Attached is a short operational playbook (novarix-lag-playbook-v1.pdf) with immediate customer-side mitigations you can try while we continue root-cause analysis. Key steps:
1) If you can tolerate slightly higher cost: switch traffic to our non-streaming completion endpoint for the heaviest interactive flows (this removes token-by-token backpressure).
2) Reduce max_tokens on conversational prompts where feasible and enforce a 2s chunk timeout on your client to avoid long idle KV cache holds.
3) Enable our documented retry/backoff: exponential backoff (250ms base, max 3 retries) for 408/429 transient responses; avoid hot-looping reconnects.
4) As a short-term fallback, pin to the companion smaller model variant (redwood-m-f16) for lower-latency tail behavior.

We want to schedule a quick 30-minute call to walk through the playbook, answer questions, and confirm whether you want us to keep the warm replica routing in place for the next 24 hours. Proposed times: today 11:30 PT or 15:00 PT.

Apologies for the disruption — we know latency in interactive features is critical. I'll continue to provide updates as we learn more.

Best,
Rachel

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the rapid response and the playbook. A couple quick clarifications: 

- We rely heavily on streaming to provide lower perceived latency for our customer chat UI. Is the non-streaming fallback likely to increase end-to-end user latency in normal conditions, or only in the degraded case?
- Our platform does aggressive aggregation on our side; we can try the 2s chunk timeout, but will that increase token counts or tokens billed?

We can do the 11:30 PT call. Also, please loop in any SRE who will be looking at the shard behavior — tagging for visibility.

—Sam

Subject: RE: Intermittent lag on interactive/chat stream — immediate mitigations & playbook

Thanks for the heads up, Rachel. A few internal notes I captured during triage: 
- Observable: elevated per-token p99 latency and increased kernel preemption on the long-seq inference workers; batching increased queue time for mixture of short + long requests.
- Current mitigation (implemented at 09:00 PT): route Novarix traffic to warm-replica pool + per-customer batch-size limit to reduce head-of-line blocking. This reduced observed 95th-latency by ~40% in initial checks.
- Next steps: we have an INF ticket (INF-4521) open to instrument client-side keepalive/idle time metrics and add a temporary heuristic to prefer model-variants that are quantization-friendly for long contexts.

Suggested customer-facing guidance (to include on the call):
1) Client: set chunk-timeout to 1.5–2s to close idle streams and free KV cache sooner.
2) Server-side fallback: toggle off streaming for super-long responses (e.g., >1200 tokens) and use non-streaming completions for those flows.
3) Quick config: enable \"graceful_fallback\": true in the SDK so when streaming hits a transient degrade, the SDK will automatically re-request a non-streaming response.

I'll join the 11:30 PT call. Vivek — can you bring a short slide of the mitigation metrics?

—Marissa
Principal CS Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Date: 2026-12-20T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call follow-up: agreed actions and expected timelines

Hi Samantha, Daniel — thanks for the call earlier. Quick written summary and owners so we have a single reference: 

Agreed immediate actions (today — 24 hours):
- Redwood: keep warm-replica routing enabled for Novarix until 09:00 PT 12/21 — OWNER: Marissa.
- Novarix: set client chunk-timeout to 2s and enable SDK graceful_fallback flag; test in staging and report results by 12/20 23:59 PT — OWNER: Daniel.
- Redwood SRE: instrument per-connection idle/keepalive metrics and add temporary telemetry in INF-4521 — OWNER: Vivek.
- Both: hybrid fallback plan — Redwood to fallback traffic to smaller variant redwood-m-f16 if p99 > 1.2s for 5m window — OWNER: Rachel (coord).

What to expect next:
- We'll follow up with a short postmortem and concrete RCA by tomorrow EOD with more detail about why batching pressure increased for long-context requests.
- If Novarix prefers, we can provide a short in-product toggle to disable streaming for specific routes while you validate.

Notes on billing/charge impact: routing to warm replicas and smaller model variant can change egress and execution cost slightly; we'll surface expected delta in the RCA.

Again, apologies for the degradation. Please reply to this thread if anything above needs correction.

Thanks — talk soon,
Rachel
